children: Adyen's new CFO, Niclas Neglen, will need to earn the confidence of investors, Jefferies analysts Hannes Leitner and Charles Brennan write. The Amsterdam-based payments provider appointed Neglen, who currently holds the role at online-payments company Karna, as its new CFO from February 2027. "While Neglen will bring some public-equity experience, the 'volatile' post-IPO period of Klarna--with shares down 65% since listing a year ago--has left initial investor reactions rather negative," they say. Shares are down 1.7% at 887.70 euros, and 35% lower over the year to date. (ian.walker@wsj.com)
